implementation_notes: The standard library ships the driver interface, not a mapper: database/sql gives *sql.DB, QueryContext and Rows.Scan, and you write the mapper as a repository type whose methods translate rows into plain domain structs and write them back through parameterised ExecContext. With no reflection-based session there is no identity map or change tracking, so the classic structure survives literally as hand-written code: one mapper per aggregate, a struct with no tags and no SQL, and mapper tests as the schema contract. Reach for sqlc or sqlx only when the SQL-to-struct boilerplate, not the mapping decision, is what costs.
pitfalls: Rows.Scan fills fields positionally: reorder the SELECT list and the mapper silently assigns the wrong values whenever the types line up.
defer rows.Close() and check rows.Err() after the loop - a leaked Rows keeps a connection out of the pool and a late error is otherwise invisible.
database/sql has no session identity: two queries for the same row yield two objects, so anything relying on object identity needs a map keyed by id in the mapper.
Nullable columns need sql.NullString/NullInt64 or pointer fields, otherwise a NULL is a Scan error at runtime.

variants.name: sqlx StructScan with db struct tags
variants.implementation_notes: sqlx adds reflection on top of database/sql: GetContext and SelectContext fill a struct from a query using db struct tags, so the mapper's loop-and-Scan boilerplate disappears and the field-name contract becomes a tag. StructScan still refuses a column with no destination field unless Unsafe() is set, which keeps schema drift loud; the tradeoff is that the domain struct now carries column names in tags, so it is slightly less persistence-ignorant than the hand-written variant.
pitfalls: A tag that falls out of sync with the column name produces a zero value (or a missing-destination error) - the failure is quiet unless the mapper surfaces the sqlx error.
Keeping StructScan's default strictness is a feature: setting Unsafe() to silence the missing-destination error removes the only schema check the mapper has.
sqlx is still stateless: no identity map, no dirty tracking, and embedded-struct tags need explicit prefixes (`db:"addr_"`).
